cases.sentence: Ни одной ___ на нас не упало и наутро.
cases.translation: Not a single bomb fell on us that morning either.
cases.explain: «Ни одной» plus the negated verb «не упало» forces the genitive — after negation the subject of an existence-type sentence stands in the genitive.

cases.translation: What is more, I am introducing a curfew.
cases.explain: «Час» is the direct object of the transitive verb «ввожу», so it takes the accusative; being inanimate, that form looks like the nominative.

cases.translation: And at the same time I am becoming president.
cases.explain: The verb «становиться» (to become) governs the instrumental for the new role: становлюсь президентом.

cases.translation: Have you still got the kubanskaya in your pocket?
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional: в кармане.

cases.translation: The passengers of the train were sitting in their own seats.
cases.explain: The preposition «по» meaning 'about, around, each in its own' governs the dative, here the dative plural местам.

cases.sentence: Я вышел на ___, сжатый со всех сторон кольцом дурацких ухмылок.
cases.translation: I went out onto the carriage platform, hemmed in on all sides by a ring of idiotic grins.
cases.explain: «На» with motion towards a place (куда?) takes the accusative: вышел на площадку.

cases.sentence: Какая-то ___ во всем королевстве, и у всех мозги набекрень.
cases.translation: Something is rotten in the whole kingdom, and everyone's brains are askew.
cases.explain: In a verbless existential sentence the thing that exists is the subject, so it stands in the nominative: какая-то гниль.

cases.sentence: И вышел из поезда, смахнув слезу ___.
cases.translation: And he got off the train, brushing away a tear with his sleeve.
cases.explain: The instrument used to perform an action goes into the instrumental case with no preposition: смахнул рукавом.

reading.ru: Ни одной бомбы на нас не упало и наутро.
reading.question: What had happened by the following morning?
options: Not a single bomb had fallen on them
The village had been bombed twice
The punitive squads had already arrived
The train had been stopped at Usad
reading.correct: Not a single bomb had fallen on them
reading.explain: The chapter opens with the news that nobody bombed them overnight either, which is why the world seems to be ignoring their revolution.

reading.question: How did the senators react when Venichka took full power and made himself president?
options: They walked out of the plenum
reading.explain: Only premier Borya S. flinched, at the word «пророки»; no one actually spoke against the seizure of power.

reading.ru: Через два часа он испустил дух на руках у министра обороны.
reading.question: Where did premier Borya S. die?
options: In the arms of the minister of defence
reading.correct: In the arms of the minister of defence
reading.explain: Two hours after flinching at the mention of prophets he gave up the ghost in the defence minister's arms.

reading.ru: Он умер от тоски и от чрезмерной склонности к обобщениям.
reading.question: What does Venichka say the premier died of?
options: Melancholy and an excessive tendency to generalise
A wound received in the fighting
Drinking the last of the Russian vodka
reading.correct: Melancholy and an excessive tendency to generalise
reading.explain: No other causes seemed to be involved, and they did not perform an autopsy because doing so would have been disgusting.

reading.ru: Чья смерть, сказано не было, но мир догадывался.
reading.question: What did the message taken by all the world's teletypes leave out?
reading.explain: The wire said only that death had occurred from natural causes; the world was left to guess whose.

reading.question: What kind of session was the 4th Plenum?
options: A session that never took place
reading.explain: It followed the premier's death, and Venichka gave his resignation speech there.

reading.ru: Точно так же и я: встаю и умываю руки.
reading.question: Which figure does Venichka model his resignation on?
reading.explain: He says he would hang a portrait of Pilate washing his hands on his children's wall, and then does exactly the same himself.

reading.ru: Я присоединился к вам просто с перепою и вопреки всякой очевидности.
reading.question: Why does Venichka say he joined the delegates in the first place?
options: Simply because of a hangover and against all evidence
Because he believed in their programme
Because he was elected by the region
reading.correct: Simply because of a hangover and against all evidence
reading.explain: He disowns the whole enterprise, saying he only ever wanted to revolutionise hearts and raise souls.

reading.ru: В Общий рынок нас никто не пустит.
reading.question: What does Venichka say about their international prospects?
options: Nobody will let them into the Common Market
The Common Market has already accepted them
The Seventh Fleet is on its way to help
reading.correct: Nobody will let them into the Common Market
reading.explain: He adds that the ships of the American Seventh Fleet will not get through and would not even want to.

reading.question: What did the delegates shout from their seats that they would be given?
options: A seat in the Common Market
reading.explain: They shout about bombers and then about Phantoms, which Venichka answers with mockery.

reading.ru: Дурак ты, Тихонов, как я погляжу!
reading.question: How does Venichka answer Tikhonov's remark that they will at least be given the devaluation of the franc?
options: He calls him a fool, while granting he is a valuable theorist
He asks him to lead the plenum
reading.correct: He calls him a fool, while granting he is a valuable theorist
reading.explain: He does not dispute Tikhonov's value as a theorist, only what comes out of his mouth.

reading.ru: Короче, я пожимаю плечами и ухожу с поста президента.
reading.question: How does Venichka end his speech to the senators?
options: By shrugging and resigning the presidency
By calling for a new offensive
reading.correct: By shrugging and resigning the presidency
reading.explain: He washes his hands like Pilate, drinks up the last of the Russian vodka in front of them and leaves for Petushki.

reading.ru: В моем сердце не было раскаяния.
reading.question: What does Venichka say about his feelings as he walks away?
options: There was no repentance in his heart
He was already planning to return
reading.correct: There was no repentance in his heart
reading.explain: He repeats the point after describing the meadows, the rose hips and the cornflowers on his way.

reading.ru: Закатилось солнце, а я все шел.
reading.question: What happens as Venichka keeps walking towards Petushki?
options: The sun goes down and he is still walking
He turns back to the plenum
He lies down in a field to sleep
reading.correct: The sun goes down and he is still walking
reading.explain: Darkness falls everywhere and Petushki is still nowhere in sight, which prompts his complaint to the Queen of Heaven.

reading.question: How does the second old man, the one with the very white face, address Venichka?
options: As a 'dear wanderer', using the feminine form
reading.correct: As a 'dear wanderer', using the feminine form
reading.explain: The old man tells him it is too late for him to marry and too early for the graveyard, and calls him «милая странница».

reading.ru: «Я вашей доброты никогда не забуду, товарищ старший лейтенант!..»
reading.question: What does the passenger getting off the train whisper into Venichka's ear?
options: That he will never forget his kindness, comrade senior lieutenant
That the next stop is Usad
That he recognises him as the president
That he should get off here too
reading.correct: That he will never forget his kindness, comrade senior lieutenant
reading.explain: The man first barks a military «Никак нет!!», then shakes his hand, thanks him by rank and leaves brushing away a tear.

highlight.question: Which sentence names what the premier died of?
sentences: Через два часа он испустил дух на руках у министра обороны.
Он умер от тоски и от чрезмерной склонности к обобщениям.
Других причин вроде бы не было, а вскрывать мы его не вскрывали, потому что вскрывать было бы противно.
А к вечеру того же дня все телетайпы мира приняли сообщение.
«Смерть наступила вследствие естественных причин».
Чья смерть, сказано не было, но мир догадывался.
highlight.explain: The second sentence gives the cause — melancholy and an excessive tendency to generalise.

highlight.question: Which sentence admits that Venichka cannot tell one kind of building from another?
sentences: «Где же Петушки?» – спросил я, подойдя к чьей-то освещенной веранде.
Откуда она взялась, эта веранда?
Может, это совсем не веранда, а терраса, мезонин или флигель? я ведь в этом ничего не понимаю и вечно путаю.
highlight.explain: The last sentence is the confession that he understands nothing about it and always gets it mixed up.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how the people on the veranda answered his question?
sentences: Я постучался и спросил: «Где же Петушки? Далеко еще до Петушков?»
А мне в ответ – все, кто был на веранде, – все расхохотались и ничего не сказали.
Я обиделся и снова постучал – ржание на веранде возобновилось.
Странно!
Мало того – кто-то ржал у меня за спиной.
highlight.explain: The second sentence reports that everyone on the veranda burst out laughing and said nothing.

highlight.question: Which sentence quotes Saadi's advice about the cypress and the palm?
sentences: «Ничего, Ерофеев, ничего.
Пусть смеются, не обращай внимания.
Как сказал Саади, будь прям и прост, как кипарис, и будь, как пальма, щедр.
Не понимаю, при чем тут пальма, ну да ладно, все равно будь, как пальма.
У тебя кубанская в кармане осталась? осталась.
Ну вот, поди на площадку и выпей.
Выпей, – чтобы не так тошнило».
highlight.explain: The third sentence is the quotation from Saadi that Venichka uses to steady himself.

highlight.question: Which sentence is where Venichka concludes that he himself, and not the old man, has gone out of his mind?
sentences: Он что, очумел, этот дед?
Какая мама?
Какие уроки?..
От какого горшка?..
Да нет, наверно, не дед очумел, а я сам очумел.
Потому что вот и другой старичок, с белым-белым лицом, стал около меня, снизу вверх посмотрел мне в глаза и сказал: – Да и вообще: куда тебе ехать?
highlight.explain: After a run of indignant questions he decides that the madness must be his own.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes Venichka physically checking himself over after being called a 'dear wanderer'?
sentences: Я вздрогнул и отошел в другой конец тамбура.
Что-то неладное в мире.
Какая-то гниль во всем королевстве, и у всех мозги набекрень.
Я на всякий случай тихонько всего себя ощупал: какая же я после этого «милая странница»?
С чего это он взял?
Да и к чему?
Можно, конечно, пошутить – но ведь не до такой же степени нелепо!
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence is the one where he quietly feels himself all over just to be sure.
